value.rationale: The no-consecutive-ones language is a natural finite-type coding constraint studied in run-length-limited deletion channels. The theorem quantifies for every length the exact difference between the induced Hamming graph and deletion-conflict graph: the extra deletion-only edge class has a separate rational generating function, dominates Hamming conflicts by a factor of order n, and yields a quadratic mean-degree law. This structural invariant matters when analyzing constrained synchronization-code conflict density, without claiming new code capacity or artificial downstream consequences.
